---
title: "Autosprint"
subtitle: "An automated sprint loop — Plan, Implement, Test, Commit."
---

Autosprint runs an autonomous **PIT loop** against a *target repository*. You
write down where you want the code to end up in `autosprint/destination.md`;
autosprint repeatedly measures the gap and closes it, one sprint at a time,
using AI agents driven by the Claude Agent SDK and the GitHub Copilot SDK.

## The PIT loop

Each sprint runs four phases:

1. **Plan** — one or more AI agents propose tasks; a selector merges them into
   `autosprint/plan.md`.
2. **Implement** — an AI agent implements the top pending task.
3. **Test** — the target repo's own test suite runs (real pytest/vitest, not an
   LLM judging itself).
4. **Commit** — if tests pass, the change is committed to the working branch.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-pit-loop
%%| fig-cap: "The four phases of a sprint. A failing Test phase reverts the working tree instead of committing."
flowchart LR
  Plan --> Implement --> Test
  Test -->|tests pass| Commit
  Test -->|tests fail| Revert
  Commit --> Plan
  Revert --> Plan
```

## What makes it safe

- **Autosprint never modifies itself.** The orchestrator refuses to run if
  `TARGET_REPO` points at the autosprint repo. All file changes happen inside
  the target repository — autosprint ships only methodology, prompts, and
  orchestration.
- **Every sprint is a transaction.** A sprint that fails its tests is reverted,
  so the working branch only ever moves forward through green states.
- **You stay in control.** A reviewed `plan.md`, optional waypoints, and a stop
  control file let you steer or halt the loop at any time.
